user_query: How does the Skip-gram objective in the model from PASSAGE A differ from the language-modeling objective in PASSAGE B in terms of what is being predicted from what?
llm_response: In the Skip-gram objective, the model predicts surrounding context words from a given center word. In the language-modeling objective, the model predicts the next word (or more generally the target word sequence) from the preceding context words. So Skip-gram goes from one word to its neighbors, while language modeling goes from context to the next token/word.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a standard distinction between Skip-gram and language-modeling objectives, and the wording is broadly correct, though I cannot verify the exact phrasing of PASSAGE A and PASSAGE B.
